budget_items.what_was_said: The storm-damaged Fitzgerald Field sign will be replaced using parks funds; the chair said she asked Chris Ruth the cost but he had not given her a figure.

A local company (Dillis) had agreed roughly two years ago to cover the cost of a new sign naming the beach house after Genevieve Nass; the chair said the project stalled and is handing it to Maryanne.

Dillis and Roy produced a prevailing-wage estimate for the skate park that came in around figures_as_heard, but it omitted town administrative/bid costs that were part of the original ballpark figure; final decisions expected in January.
The chair said she thought about figures_as_heard remained but it turned out closer to a lower figure; remaining money comes from ARPA (a smaller amount) and from town-meeting-approved capital funds.
A board member said the town needs to understand its finances before pushing a project of that scale forward again at town meeting.

The vacant rec director position is a 19-hour-a-week job with no benefits; a member said covering the paperwork duties falls outside the volunteer commission's purview and suggested a stipend for whoever takes it on.

budget_items.topic: Youth sports per-player field use fee
budget_items.what_was_said: The commission charges youth leagues a flat per-player fee for a season rather than an hourly rate like the school uses; figures were recalled for comparison but the board confirmed no fee change this spring.

decisions.decision: Chair will tell Chris Ruth to go ahead and replace the Fitzgerald Field sign as long as the price is reasonable, aiming for a more permanent design.
Maryanne will take over the beach house sign and dedication project from the chair, who will forward prior graphics and pricing information.
No decision on Marshall Park tonight; the chair will bring information back to the town manager in January rather than deciding in December.
The board will table further discussion of recruiting/electing new commission members and the Marshall Park path forward until closer to January.
Chair will bring a formal vote to the January agenda seeking permission to personally process field-use paperwork if the recreation director position remains unfilled.
No change to youth sports per-player field use fees this spring season.
Chair will draft revised field-use forms and bring them to an upcoming meeting in January or February.
Next meeting set for January 28th (the fourth Wednesday).

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission set aside the large Marshall Park project until the town's overall financial picture is clearer, with no work moving forward before January.
The commission will replace the storm-damaged Fitzgerald Field sign using parks funds once a cost is confirmed as reasonable.
A newer member took over the long-stalled beach house dedication sign project, honoring Genevieve Nass.
The commission kept youth sports per-player field fees unchanged for the spring season.
With the recreation director post still vacant, the chair plans to seek a formal vote in January to personally handle field-use paperwork in the meantime.

why_it_matters: Marshall Park's future, and any request for town-meeting funding, is on hold until the board revisits it in January -- residents should not expect a spring vote on the project.
The vacant, part-time recreation director position is affecting basic field-use administration, which could delay scheduling or policy fixes for youth leagues.
Youth sports families and leagues will pay the same per-player field fee this season, with written field-use policies still being drafted.
